summary: Dieuke Gaastra was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University, receiving a PhD in 1906 under Willem Caland. Gaastra also studied under Johan Hendrik Gallée.

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991, and taught numerous prominent students.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He taught at Calcutta, the University of Delhi, and Visva-Bharati University, before serving as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Archaeology at Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and held posts at the University of Calcutta and Visva-Bharati University.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) was an Indology and history scholar who earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D. Litt. from Patna University in 1961. He also taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held posts at Ohio State University (around 1999–2003) and Virginia Commonwealth University (around 2003–2017).

Dina Johanna Kohlbrugge (1911–1999) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. She earned her PhD from Utrecht University in 1938 under Jan Gonda, and served there as Professor of Modern Persian (1949) and Iranian language and literature (1956–1981).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen (1892), studying under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and served there as Docent (1901) and Professor (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (ending 1961) and held positions at the University of Calcutta, including Carmichael Professor from 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She received her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. She studied under Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw from around 1967 to 1970, and taught Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, Jack Kornfield, and Sylvia Boorstein.
Dipak Bhattacharya is an Indologist who held posts at Visva-Bharati University and Leiden University (1981–1982).

Dipak Kumar Barua is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was appointed Assistant Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and served as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from around 1996 to 1998.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. Das held posts at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipankar Bhattacharya works in Indology and linguistics. He studied for a PhD at the National Sanskrit University (2023–2026) and was appointed Project Manager (Content & Research) at Rishihood University in 2025.

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who earned a PhD from the Australian National University. He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1985–1995) and became the Lawrence A. Kimpton Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.
Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University. He served at Leiden as lecturer (1967) and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.
Dirk Huizinga (1840–1903) studied at the University of Groningen from around 1858 to 1867 and held a post there between 1870 and 1901.

Dirk Jan Hoens (1920–2003) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, completing a PhD (1951) and Dr.Theol. (1955), and worked there as an assistant from 1948 to 1982.
Dirk Schmidt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied for a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he also served as a PhD student and teaching assistant in 2022.
